tasks.label: Build Maize v2 (mzvm, mzasm), install it to ~/bin, and run its fixtures
tasks.detail: Build the v2 machine (mzvm, mzvmg), the v2 assembler (mzasm), and both fixture binaries, copy mzvm, mzvmg, mzasm and SDL2.dll to ~/bin so they are runnable from any directory, then run the v2 fixtures. This is the fast v2 loop and it is what Ctrl+Shift+B runs. The install step is what this task was missing until maize-454: the build went green and mzasm was still not on PATH. It does NOT touch the C cross-toolchain (cproc/qbe) and builds no v1 binary; the toolchain refresh lives in the Install task below. It assumes the preset's build directory is already configured; if it is not, run one of the install or build-world tasks once first. Every target the v2 ctest label needs must be named here: the ctest step invokes the fixture binaries by path, so a fixture whose target is missing reports Not Run rather than failing to build (maize-435). Fixtures run last so their result is the last thing on screen, and a red fixture still leaves you the binaries you just built. mzvm has no device surface yet, so its output is the register dump from --registers rather than anything a program prints.

windows.command: cmake --build build/windows-llvm-mingw-debug --target mzvm mzvmg mzasm mzvm_v2_fixtures mzasm_tests && powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ${workspaceFolder}/scripts/install-mzasm.ps1 -Preset windows-llvm-mingw-debug && ctest --test-dir build/windows-llvm-mingw-debug -L v2 --output-on-failure

linux.command: cmake --build build/linux-debug --target mzvm mzvmg mzasm mzvm_v2_fixtures mzasm_tests && ${workspaceFolder}/scripts/install-mzasm.sh linux-debug && ctest --test-dir build/linux-debug -L v2 --output-on-failure

osx.command: cmake --build build/macos-debug --target mzvm mzvmg mzasm mzvm_v2_fixtures mzasm_tests && ${workspaceFolder}/scripts/install-mzasm.sh macos-debug && ctest --test-dir build/macos-debug -L v2 --output-on-failure

tasks.label: Assemble current .mazm
tasks.detail: Run mazm on the active file; errors land in the Problems panel and are click-to-navigate.

tasks.label: Check current .mazm (no output file)
tasks.detail: mazm --check on the active file: same clickable errors, zero filesystem effects (no .mzb written, stale .mzb kept).

tasks.label: Assemble current .mzasm
tasks.detail: Run mzasm on the active file; errors land in the Problems panel and are click-to-navigate. This is the Maize v2 assembler, beside the v1 pair above rather than replacing them: two machines, two tools, no inference from the file suffix.

tasks.label: Check current .mzasm (no output file)
tasks.detail: mzasm --check on the active file: same clickable errors, zero filesystem effects (nothing written, nothing removed).

tasks.label: Build everything (build-world)
tasks.detail: Build the native binaries + tools, the C cross toolchain, quesOS, the wave-1 userland, and the demos, all in one call. Slower than the binaries-only install task below; run it after a fresh clone or pull. On Windows this runs natively via Git Bash, no WSL involved.

tasks.label: Install mzvm + mzvmg + mzasm + the C cross-toolchain to ~/bin
tasks.detail: Build an optimized release of the Maize v2 machine (mzvm console, mzvmg graphical/SDL) and the v2 assembler (mzasm), copy them plus SDL2.dll to the user bin directory, and refresh the C cross-toolchain (cproc/qbe + Maize target) plus mzcc, which the default Ctrl+Shift+B task deliberately does not do. Run this after pulling, or whenever mzcc needs to be current; use Build everything (build-world) for the full "I pulled" rebuild. The frozen v1 binaries (maize, maizeg, mazm) are no longer built or installed (maize-454), and mzld/mzdis wait for their v2 ports. On Windows this runs natively via Git Bash, no WSL involved.
